v.rationale: All three suites pass and all three follow the same correct pattern: a transaction around the reply insert and counter increment, then mail and notifications only after commit. They differ in mention parsing and code quality. impl-1 ranks first. It has the cleanest structure (Thread::addReply plus a NotifyMentionedUsers action, make/associate) and the most thorough tests, including a rollback when the counter increment fails and a mailable render test. Its factory generates usernames that match its regex; its remaining flaws ('@@bob' counts as a mention, no dotted usernames) are minor. impl-3 has the most correct mention parser and passed every probe, but it puts all the logic in the controller, makes reply_count mass-assignable, uses array_* functions instead of collections, and adds Queueable/SerializesModels ceremony. impl-2 is nearly as clean as impl-1, but its faker userName() factory produces dotted usernames its \w regex can't match. Only 12 of 30 factory users could be mentioned, and '@smith.john' notified a different user, 'smith': a real wrong-recipient bug. All probe test files were deleted afterwards.
